subject: English
topic: One Word Substitution — Meanings and Definitions (W10)

questions.stem: A person who cannot read or write.
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Illiterate' specifically means unable to read or write. Trap: 'Ignorant' means lacking knowledge in general (not specifically literacy); 'Naive' means simple or innocent; 'Introvert' describes a shy or inward person — none of these relate specifically to reading/writing ability.

A is correct. 'Calligraphy' comes from Greek kallos (beauty) + graphia (writing) — the art of producing decorative, beautiful handwriting. Trap: 'Typography' is the art of arranging printed type (not handwriting); 'Lithography' is a printing technique; 'Photography' records images with light.

questions.stem: A speech delivered without prior preparation or notes.
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Extempore' (from Latin ex tempore = out of the moment) means spoken without preparation, on the spur of the moment. Trap: 'Eulogy' is a speech in praise of someone (often a funeral speech); 'Soliloquy' is a theatrical device where a character speaks thoughts aloud; 'Monologue' is a long speech by one person but may be prepared.

B is correct. 'Acrophobia' = fear of heights (acro- = peak/top). Trap: 'Claustrophobia' = fear of enclosed spaces; 'Agoraphobia' = fear of open or crowded public spaces; 'Hydrophobia' = fear of water (also a symptom of rabies). SSC regularly tests the phobia vocabulary — acro/claustro/agora/hydro are the four most tested.

questions.stem: An animal that eats both plants and other animals.
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Omnivore' = eats both plant and animal matter (omni- = all). Trap: 'Carnivore' = eats only meat; 'Herbivore' = eats only plants; 'Insectivore' = eats insects. Humans are omnivores; lions are carnivores; cows are herbivores.

questions.stem: The branch of linguistics concerned with the origin and historical development of words.
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Etymology' studies the origin and historical development of words (etymon = true sense of a word, in Greek). Trap: 'Phonology' studies the sound systems of language; 'Lexicology' studies vocabulary and word meaning (synchronic, not historical); 'Morphology' studies word structure and forms (prefixes, roots, suffixes).

questions.stem: A person who pretends to have religious virtues or moral beliefs that they do not actually possess.
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Hypocrite' = one who feigns virtue or moral correctness while privately behaving otherwise. Trap: 'Agnostic' = one who believes nothing can be known about God's existence (no moral pretence implied); 'Atheist' = one who disbelieves in God (openly, not pretending); 'Apostate' = one who abandons their religion (an act of leaving, not pretending).

questions.stem: A remedy or solution believed to cure all diseases or solve all problems.
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Panacea' = a universal remedy for all ills (from Greek pan = all + akeia = remedy; also the name of the goddess of healing). Trap: 'Antidote' counteracts a specific poison; 'Placebo' is an inert substance that produces psychological improvement; 'Vaccine' prevents specific diseases through immunity — none are universal solutions.

questions.stem: The act of killing one's own father.
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Patricide' = killing of one's father (pater = father). Trap: 'Parricide' is broader — killing of either parent or a close relative; 'Matricide' = killing of one's mother (mater); 'Fratricide' = killing of one's brother (frater). SSC tests the -cide words frequently: patricide/matricide/fratricide/infanticide/homicide/regicide.

questions.stem: The policy of extending a nation's power and influence through military force, colonization, or economic domination over other territories.
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Imperialism' = the policy of extending a country's power over others through conquest or dominance (empire-building). Trap: 'Nationalism' = devotion to one's own nation (internal pride, not expansion); 'Socialism' = collective ownership of production (economic philosophy); 'Federalism' = division of power between central and regional governments (structural governance).
